related_questions.question: What are the risks of the COVID vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 vaccines, like any vaccine, carry some risks, though serious side effects are rare. The most common side effects are mild and temporary, such as pain or swelling at the injection site, fever, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, and nausea. More serious side effects, such as anaphylaxis (a severe allergic reaction) and myocarditis/pericarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle or lining), are very rare. The risk of these serious side effects is generally outweighed by the benefits of vaccination in preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19.

list.title: Anaphylaxis:
list.snippet: A severe allergic reaction that can occur after any vaccine. Symptoms include wheezing, difficulty breathing, low blood pressure, or hives. It's treatable with epinephrine (EpiPen) and usually requires hospitalization.

list.title: Myocarditis and Pericarditis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the heart muscle or lining, particularly seen in young men after mRNA vaccines (Pfizer and Moderna). Most cases are mild and resolve on their own, according to the FDA.
COVID-19 vaccines are highly effective at preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death from COVID-19.
The risk of serious side effects from the vaccines is very low, especially when compared to the risks associated with contracting COVID-19.
The CDC and FDA have ongoing surveillance systems to monitor vaccine safety and identify any potential risks.
The FDA has updated the warnings on mRNA COVID-19 vaccines to include information about the risk of myocarditis and pericarditis.
The FDA has conducted benefit-risk assessments for the vaccines, including in specific age groups and for different variants, to ensure their continued safety and effectiveness.
